editorial:
Ever feel like your life is just a mess of bad timing and weird habits? You will totally relate to the group of people in this flick. It follows six different folks in New York City who are all just trying to figure things out. You get to meet Zeke and Luke, who work in a sex shop and have totally opposite views on life, and Stephen, who seems to have it all but is actually quite lonely. Then you have Peter, who is way too obsessed with cleaning, and Derek, who is just too nice for his own good. To top it off, there is Marilyn, who is trying to stay sober while planning a wedding that is stressing her out. The whole vibe is like hanging out with a group of friends who are all slightly falling apart but still trying their best.

What really makes this work is how natural the dialogue feels. You will laugh at the awkward dates and the fights over apartment chores because it feels real. While the pacing is a bit slow in the middle, the chemistry between the actors keeps you interested. If you love stories about messy relationships and city life, you should definitely give this a shot. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you really love the cast, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep it. It is a sweet, funny look at how hard it is to be an adult.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that nobody has their life perfectly figured out, and that is okay. Luke and Stephen move past their stereotypes and find a real connection. Peter and Derek learn to compromise on their living habits so they can actually stay together. Marilyn finally stops obsessing over the wedding and focuses on her own health. Everyone ends up in a better place by accepting their flaws and being honest with the people they love.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky romantic comedies about urban life.
